path_base: wiki/papers/analysis/ (all relative paths resolve from this directory)
review_status_definition: reviewed = full-text reading by assigned analyst, editorial/structural checks, and targeted source spot-checks; not experimental reproduction or independent verification of every claim
draft_status_definition: draft = full-text reading by one assigned analyst plus structural checks and a targeted quote and number spot-check; no second-reader review yet (entries 23-33, added 2026-11-21)

entries.title: KernelBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient GPU Kernels?
entries.summary: Introduces 250 PyTorch-defined kernel-generation tasks and the correctness-gated fast_p metric, with one-shot, sampling, feedback, and hardware-context experiments.

entries.title: KernelBenchX: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
entries.summary: Category-aware evaluation of Triton generation separates compilation, semantic correctness, repair dynamics, and performance across 176 tasks and six GPUs.

entries.title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch?
entries.summary: Re-evaluates generated KernelBench candidates using TF32-enabled eager baselines, transformed hidden inputs, memory metrics, and a residual-hack code audit.

entries.title: PTXBench: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for GPU Kernel Optimization with Architecture-specific PTX
entries.summary: PTXBench tests runtime use of architecture-specific GPU instructions separately from correctness and speed, and studies repair-conditioned adaptation of Qwen3.6-27B.

entries.title: TritonBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Capabilities for Generating Triton Operators
entries.summary: Dual-channel Triton benchmark contrasts 184 curated GitHub operators with 166 PyTorch-interface tasks using correctness, latency, and hardware-efficiency measurements.

entries.title: MultiKernelBench: A Multi-Platform Benchmark for Kernel Generation
entries.summary: MultiKernelBench evaluates 285 PyTorch-defined tasks on CUDA, AscendC, and Pallas, exposing platform/category differences and testing category-specific exemplars.

entries.title: ISO-Bench: Can Coding Agents Optimize Real-World Inference Workloads?
entries.summary: ISO-Bench evaluates agent patches on 54 inference-serving optimization tasks using human-relative performance, judge-rated bottleneck targeting, and selective functional validation.

entries.title: Towards Robust Agentic CUDA Kernel Benchmarking, Verification, and Optimization
entries.summary: Introduces robust-kbench and an evolutionary CUDA search pipeline with prompt-tuned LLM screening, measuring benchmark loopholes, forward/backward optimization, and shape/hardware generalization while retaining empirical hardware checks.

entries.title: Bit-Accurate Modeling of GPU Matrix Multiply-Accumulate Units: Demystifying Numerical Discrepancy and Accuracy
entries.summary: CLFP derives and differentially tests instruction-level arithmetic models for ten GPU architectures, explaining mixed-precision discrepancies and identifying precision bottlenecks, rounding bias and targeted workarounds.

entries.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
entries.summary: Studies how search, file viewing, editing guardrails, and context management affect fixed-model software-engineering agents on SWE-bench and HumanEvalFix.

entries.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
entries.summary: Introduces interleaved language reasoning and environment actions, testing prompted and fine-tuned variants on knowledge reasoning and interactive decision tasks.

entries.title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
entries.summary: Trains 7B/13B rubric-conditioned evaluators on synthetic feedback and studies reference materials, human agreement, distribution shift, and preference ranking.

entries.title: From Generation to Judgment: Opportunities and Challenges of LLM-as-a-judge
entries.summary: Survey taxonomy of judge inputs, outputs, six assessment attributes, training and prompting methods, four application areas, benchmark families, and unresolved bias, efficiency, and robustness problems.

entries.title: Lessons from the Trenches on Reproducible Evaluation of Language Models
entries.summary: Documents evaluation failure modes and reproducibility practices, with prompt-format case studies and formal descriptions of likelihood, perplexity, and generative scoring.

entries.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
entries.summary: Prompted NLG evaluation using generated evaluation steps and probability-weighted scores, tested against human judgments on summarization and dialogue.

entries.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
entries.summary: Introduces MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena and measures how LLM judges align with human preferences under explicit tie-handling and bias controls.

entries.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
entries.summary: A study of response-order bias in pairwise LLM judging, with evidence-first sampling, balanced positions, and entropy-based human review.

entries.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
entries.summary: Tests a same-model generate–critique–revise loop across seven tasks, with strong task-dependent gains and a major bottleneck in detecting incorrect feedback.

entries.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
entries.summary: Reflexion converts trial feedback into bounded textual memories for subsequent attempts, with gains and failures across ALFWorld, HotpotQA, and code generation that depend strongly on evaluation quality.

entries.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
entries.summary: Learns API-call placement and arguments by filtering sampled tool annotations for next-token loss improvement, with controlled tool-disabled and decoding-policy evaluations.

entries.title: Measuring Automated Kernel Engineering
entries.summary: METR evaluates a tree-search kernel agent on a filtered, extended KernelBench suite, reporting speedups and cost tradeoffs while documenting major gaps from expert kernel engineering.

entries.title: LARK: Lean-Assisted Reasoning for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
entries.summary: LARK uses Lean-checked race-freedom, segmentation and equivalence proofs to certify supported GPU kernels relative to a pinned machine model and task interface, while leaving floating-point fidelity and host-allocation safety outside its theorem.

entries.title: TensorLean: Formal Verification of Production GPU Kernels
entries.summary: TensorLean is announced as a Lean/SMT framework proving that compiled PTX meets a tensor-level real-number specification within a stated tolerance on every input and schedule; all results are unreplicated author claims with no released artifact or paper at snapshot.

entries.title: K-Search: LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model
entries.summary: K-Search has an LLM maintain a search tree of optimization intents and instantiates each by sampling evaluator-scored kernels; evidence is four FlashInfer kernels (three runs per method) and one TriMul task, with trace-based correctness testing and no ablations.

entries.title: FlashInfer-Bench: Building the Virtuous Cycle for AI-driven LLM Systems
entries.summary: FlashInfer-Bench defines a JSON Trace schema, a serving-derived kernel dataset, a tolerance-gated benchmark and an apply() dispatcher for LLM-generated GPU kernels; tolerance values are unstated, and its one end-to-end test shows no generated kernel beating FlashInfer.

entries.title: VERINA: Benchmarking Verifiable Code Generation
entries.summary: VERINA is a 189-task Lean 4 benchmark for code, specification and proof generation; specifications are scored mostly by tests against a ground-truth specification, and single-trial proof success is at most 4.9% for general-purpose models.

entries.title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
entries.summary: Audits SWE-Perf, GSO and SWE-fficiency by replaying 740 reference patches on four Google Cloud CPU machine types and re-scoring public submissions, finding unstable reference signals and scoring-rule-dependent rankings; it covers repository-level CPU benchmarks, not GPU kernels.

entries.title: AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions
entries.summary: AuXSpec pairs each declarative Lean postcondition with an executable Boolean check so frozen test cases can score generated specifications and reward RL training; test agreement plus LLM judges is evidence of intent capture, not proof, on LeetCode-style problems.

entries.title: ClarifyGPT: Empowering LLM-based Code Generation with Intention Clarification
entries.summary: ClarifyGPT flags a requirement as ambiguous when sampled solutions disagree on generated test inputs, asks targeted questions and regenerates code; Pass@1 gains on HumanEval/MBPP use answers from humans or an LLM that both see ground-truth tests.

entries.title: KernelFoundry: Hardware-aware evolutionary GPU kernel optimization
entries.summary: KernelFoundry combines a 64-cell MAP-Elites kernel archive, transition-derived mutation hints, meta-prompt evolution and templated parameter tuning for SYCL and CUDA kernels; results rest on sampled relative-tolerance correctness and report no repeated runs or variance estimates.

entries.title: CudaForge: An Agent Framework with Hardware Feedback for CUDA Kernel Optimization
entries.summary: CudaForge is a training-free Coder–Judge loop that feeds test errors and a 24-metric Nsight Compute subset to an LLM Judge to optimize KernelBench CUDA kernels; evidence is single-run, fixed-test, 1e-4-tolerance speedup over PyTorch, mostly with OpenAI-o3.

entries.title: Kevin: Multi-Turn RL for Generating CUDA Kernels
entries.summary: Kevin fine-tunes QwQ-32B with multi-turn GRPO on 180 KernelBench Level 1-2 tasks and reports 82% best@16 correctness and 1.10x mean speedup on 100 held-out tasks, measured at fixed input sizes on H200 GPUs with 16 trajectories of 8 turns.

entries.title: Robust benchmarking in noisy environments
entries.summary: Models CPU timing noise as non-negative delays, argues for the minimum as run-time estimator, and gives a heuristic for executions per measurement in Julia's BenchmarkTools; evidence is four Julia microbenchmarks on undescribed hardware, with no decision rule or GPU analysis.

question_routes.name: Kernel benchmark design and metrics
question_routes.scope: Task definitions, baselines, sampling budgets, correctness gates, performance aggregation, and hardware/task coverage.

question_routes.name: Correctness, numerical behavior, and proof boundaries
question_routes.scope: Hidden tests, runtime instruction checks, soft verification, hardware floating-point models, and formal proof assumptions.

question_routes.name: Agents, tools, and iterative improvement
question_routes.scope: Agent interfaces, reasoning/action loops, self-feedback, episodic memory, and learned API selection.

question_routes.name: Kernel search and optimization feedback
question_routes.scope: Execution/profiler feedback, refinement trajectories, candidate selection, repository optimization, and resource budgets.

question_routes.name: LLM judges, rubrics, and bias
question_routes.scope: Judge training, scoring protocols, agreement measures, order/verbosity/self-preference effects, and survey navigation.

question_routes.name: Reproducible evaluation and comparison conditions
question_routes.scope: Prompt/metric implementation, uncertainty, baseline configuration, tie handling, denominators, and aggregation.

question_routes.name: Inference optimization in larger systems
question_routes.scope: Repository patches, application-level extrapolation, production-kernel adaptation, and limits of benchmark-to-deployment inference.

question_routes.name: Requirement clarification and formal specifications
question_routes.scope: Ambiguity detection, clarifying questions, writing and checking Lean specifications, and what a specification or proof leaves trusted.
